validated_results.title: Genetic susceptibility of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) gene C677T, A1298C, and G1793A polymorphisms with risk for bladder transitional cell carcinoma in men.
validated_results.reason: The analysis targets MTHFR C677T, A1298C, and G1793A genotypes and haplotypes for bladder cancer risk, with serum vitamin B12 only measured and no population-wide vitamin B12–bladder cancer incidence estimate reported.

validated_results.title: Genetic susceptibility of methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) gene C677T, A1298C, and G1793A polymorphisms with risk for bladder transitional cell carcinoma in men.
validated_results.reason: For transitional cell carcinoma the reported risk estimates are all genotype- or haplotype-based, and no separable vitamin B12 exposure effect on urothelial carcinoma risk is provided.

validated_results.title: Genetic polymorphisms of glutathione S-transferase M1 and bladder cancer risk: a meta-analysis of 26 studies.
validated_results.reason: This is a meta-analysis of 26 case-control studies of GSTM1 polymorphism rather than an original study of nutritional glutathione exposure.

validated_results.title: Genetic polymorphisms of glutathione S-transferase P1 and bladder cancer susceptibility in a Chinese population.
validated_results.reason: The exposure is the GSTP1 A1578G genetic polymorphism, a genotype concept rather than nutritional glutathione intake or a glutathione biomarker.

validated_results.title: Calcium and magnesium in drinking water and risk of death from kidney cancer.
validated_results.journal: Journal of toxicology and environmental health. Part A
validated_results.reason: The outcome is death attributed to kidney cancer in a mortality case-control design comparing kidney cancer deaths with deaths from other causes, not incident kidney cancer.

validated_results.title: Calcium and magnesium in drinking water and risk of death from kidney cancer.
validated_results.journal: Journal of toxicology and environmental health. Part A
validated_results.reason: Magnesium levels in drinking water were assessed against kidney cancer mortality rather than incident kidney cancer.
